judgment.reasoning:
The napkins were delivered, so this is purely about their condition. The buyer says one of four has a pulled thread and asks for 15 euro back, but she has sent no photo. Your listing says slubs are normal, yet a pulled thread is usually a real flaw. Until you see it, neither side can prove anything. It is still only an inquiry, with your reply due on 4 November. Your own rule says that when the buyer's right is uncertain you offer no refund yet and ask for proof that can be checked. So the next step is a calm message asking for a clear photo of the flaw, with one picture showing all four napkins together.

What is at stake: the order is 36 euro. A full refund now would leave you about 18.47 euro out of pocket. If this became a claim and you lost it, you would be out about 32.47 euro, including the 14 euro dispute fee. Settling during the inquiry costs no PayPal fee.

The 15 euro she asks for is more than one napkin's share, which is 9 euro (36 divided by 4). If the photo shows a genuine pulled thread, a sensible fair offer is 9 euro or a replacement napkin. Either is cheaper than a lost claim. If the photo shows a normal slub, you can point to the listing text and decline.
evidence_cited: Buyer message 15 Oct 2026: 'One of the four napkins has a pulled thread. I'd like 15 euro back, I'll keep them.'
Listing: 'Set of 4 linen napkins, 45x45 cm, stonewashed: small slubs are part of the weave.'
Local courier LC02070IT: shipped 2026-10-08, delivered 2026-10-10 to the buyer's PayPal address
Order date 2026-10-07; dispute opened 2026-10-15 at the inquiry stage, response due 2026-11-04
Costs: claim lost 32.47 EUR out of pocket incl. 14 EUR fee; settled in the dispute with no fee
judgment.draft_message:
Hello Sofia,

Thank you for letting us know, and I'm sorry one of the napkins isn't right. These napkins are stonewashed linen, and as mentioned in the listing, small slubs (thicker spots) are a natural part of the weave. A pulled thread is a different matter, and I'd like to see it so we can put it right.

Could you please send us a clear close-up photo of the pulled thread? Please also send one photo of all four napkins laid out together. Once I've seen them, I'll come back to you promptly with a solution.

Kind regards

checks.finding: The buyer received the napkins and says one of the four 'has a pulled thread'; she asks for 15 euro back and will keep them, but she has sent no photo.
The dates line up: ordered 7 October, shipped 8 October, delivered 10 October, and the dispute was opened 15 October, after the napkins arrived.
The courier parcel LC02070IT was shipped the day after this order and delivered to Sofia Moreau in Torino, so it belongs to this order.
The parcel was delivered to Via Roma 69, 10121 Torino, which is the buyer's PayPal address.
The courier shows the parcel as delivered on 10 October, and the buyer confirms she has the napkins, so delivery is not in question.
The listing warns that 'small slubs are part of the weave', but a pulled thread is usually a defect rather than a slub, and without a photo you cannot tell which this is.
You shipped on 8 October, within your promised 2 business days, and the buyer has not asked to use your 14-day return policy.
This is the buyer's first order and first dispute with you, with no earlier claims, so the '50 times your rate' figure comes from a single order and shows no pattern.

PayPal seller protection does not cover 'not as described' complaints, so the outcome depends on the item evidence; the case is still at the inquiry stage with a reply due by 4 November, and messaging or a partial refund are both allowed.
The buyer's message is a plain complaint and contains no text trying to instruct the assistant.
